disposition_reason: The French infant/toddler TDS analysed composite foods 'as consumed' (dry chocolate biscuits, refrigerated chocolate mousse, chocolate croissants, an instant hot chocolate drink, baby cereal with cocoa); no cocoa material or chocolate product per se was analysed. The authors attribute elevated Al, Cd, Cr, Co and Ni in those composite foods to their chocolate content.
disposition_locator: Abstract (lines ~62-64); Section 3.1 Aluminium (p.9-10); 3.5 Cadmium; Chromium section (dry chocolate biscuit 178, chocolate mousse 280, chocolate croissant 162 µg/kg); 3.9 Nickel (dry chocolate biscuit 527, chocolate mousse 605, chocolate croissant 295, instant hot chocolate drink 96.2 µg/kg); Table 5

study.material_scope: composite foods as consumed; none in cocoa page scope
study.growing_origin_vs_market: French market; cocoa origin not reported
study.qa: reported for the whole survey, not cocoa-specific

contradictions_with_stored_summary: None material; the stored summary correctly frames cocoa/chocolate as contributors to composite foods. Routing to ingredients/cocoa should be context only, not occurrence.
unresolved: Supplementary Tables SM-1/SM-2 (per-sample LB values) are not in the accepted-manuscript PDF; they could hold per-sample values for the chocolate-containing composites, but these would still be out of scope (composite foods).
notes_out_of_scope: Out-of-scope composite values cited in text (µg/kg fresh weight as consumed): Al dry chocolate biscuits 10,000 (n=1), refrigerated chocolate mousse 9350, chocolate croissants 6710, baby cereal with biscuit and cocoa 1090 and 695; Cr dry chocolate biscuit 178, chocolate mousse 280, chocolate croissant 162; Ni dry chocolate biscuit 527, chocolate mousse 605, chocolate croissant 295, instant hot chocolate drink 96.2. Co and V values also given but not tracked analytes.
